Given the graph of $y=f(x)$ above, find the value of 
${\int }_{-4}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The graph consists of $2$ parts: the arc of the semi-circle for $x\in [-4,0]$ and the line segment for $x\in (0,3).$ So, we can use the additive property of integrals to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-4}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{3}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={{{\int }_{-4}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{0}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-4,0].$ The corresponding region is a combination of a semi-circle of radius $2$ and a rectangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}(\pi {r}^{2})+bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\pi \cdot {2}^{2})+4(2) \\  & =2\pi +8.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (0,3).$ The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1+3)(3) \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2} \\  & =(2\pi +8)+6 \\  & =2\pi +14.\end{aligned}
$$
